html:
SMTO-JOB-0009 — SMTO couldn't set up or change this timed wait

GUID: e771e253-53cf-4700-ac1b-5d99795cc06e
Slug: wait-schedule-invalid
Domain: JOB · Subsystem: job

What happened

  • The task asked to pause until a time or an event, or you tried to shift a wait, but the request didn't give one clear, valid amount of time or event. No wait was created or changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If you used the time controls next to a waiting task, enter a whole number of 1 or more, choose seconds, minutes or hours, then select + or −. SMTO only shifts a wait by a real, nonzero amount of time that stays within a valid date.
  2. If you just want the task to continue now, select Wake now instead of changing the time. Wake now ends the timed wait without needing any amount of time.
  3. If the agent set the wait, reply in the conversation with one clear instruction, for example "wait 10 minutes, then continue". The agent can then ask for a single valid delay instead of mixing a time with an event.

What success looks like

  • The task shows it is waiting with a countdown, or it continues after you select Wake now.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't submit the same wait again unchanged; it will be refused the same way.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Wait validation rejected the request: a time wait needs exactly one of wake_at or a positive finite delay_seconds and no event_id, an event wait needs an event_id and no time fields, or a wait adjustment was zero, non-finite or outside the supported date range.

What this means

  • Wait validation mixes event/time fields, omits an exclusive wake_at/delay value, supplies a non-finite number, or uses a nonpositive/overflowing relative delay. Job identity, supervision and dispatch/terminal receipts own effect truth. Diagnostics do not launch, cancel or replay work; missing output or failed control does not prove that the original process stopped.

Why this can happen

  • Wait validation mixes event/time fields, omits an exclusive wake_at/delay value, supplies a non-finite number, or uses a nonpositive/overflowing relative delay.

How to diagnose it

  • Distinguish absolute wake_at from positive relative delay_seconds and event_id; a past absolute time has different semantics from a negative delay.

How to fix it

  • For wait_for_event with kind=time, send exactly one of wake_at (finite epoch seconds) or delay_seconds (positive and finite) and omit event_id; for event waits send an observed event_id and omit wake_at and delay_seconds. For a wait adjustment (wait_control.apply), send action=adjust with a finite nonzero delta_seconds, or action=wake with no delta.
  • For kind=time supply exactly one supported wake_at or positive finite delay_seconds. For an event wait supply an observed event_id and omit time-only fields.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • One supported finite time or exact scoped event is accepted by the wait owner.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Job identity, supervision and dispatch/terminal receipts own effect truth. Diagnostics do not launch, cancel or replay work; missing output or failed control does not prove that the original process stopped.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
